title: Quarterly Stage-Gate & Resource Sprint Grid — regional launch calendar orchestration
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Purpose: Define and roll out a repeatable quarter-level stage-gate process plus a resource sprint grid that coordinates runtime, Console, and API releases across NA/EU/APAC launch windows. The goal is to reduce last-minute resource contention, make gate decisions observable, and provide clear preflight criteria for canary and for regional cutovers. Scope: tooling (calendar-as-code template + dashboard), playbooks for stage-gate criteria (capacity, SLO delta, regression risk), and a small Console UX change to show per-region go/no-go badges. Out of scope: infra-level autoscaling engine changes; those will be handled as follow-up work if capacity thresholds require it.
acceptance_criteria: Calendar-as-code template that generates per-quarter launch lanes with region tags
Stage-gate checklist integrated into the launch dashboard with pass/fail signals
Resource sprint grid mapping owners, critical PRs, and runbook owners for each launch lane
Pilot run on runtime-1.20 canary for NA and EU lanes with documented decision outcomes
risks: Kernel selection regressions during canary could push rollbacks and invalidate downstream Console checks
Insufficient preflight telemetry for APAC regions leading to conservative cutoff decisions
Cross-team dependency friction (SDK/runtime/infra) if owners aren’t clearly aligned in the grid
tradeoffs: Automating stage-gate signals requires higher telemetry retention (cost) vs. manual signoff which is slower but cheaper
Tighter regional windows improve safety but reduce flexibility for customer-facing releases
Adding Console badges increases UI complexity; chosen lightweight approach is a read-only badge rather than full gating UI
